title: Oklahoma's 2010 NFL Draft: Three Sooners in the First Four Picks
question: Which school had three players taken in the first four picks of the 2010 NFL Draft?
answer: Oklahoma. In 2010 Sam Bradford went No. 1 to St. Louis, Gerald McCoy No. 3 to Tampa Bay and Trent Williams No. 4 to Washington, making OU the first school in NFL Draft history with three of the first four picks.
summary: In 2010 Oklahoma became the first school with three of the NFL Draft's first four picks: Sam Bradford, Gerald McCoy and Trent Williams. Here is the story.
body: April 22, 2010, belonged to Oklahoma. In the first NFL Draft ever held in prime time, at Radio City Music Hall, three of the first four players to walk across the stage were Sooners. Only Nebraska's Ndamukong Suh, taken second by Detroit, broke up the crimson run.

Quarterback Sam Bradford (OU 2006-09) went first overall to the St. Louis Rams. Defensive tackle Gerald McCoy (OU 2006-09), an Oklahoma City product, went third to Tampa Bay, and tackle Trent Williams (OU 2006-09) went fourth to Washington. All three attended the draft in person, something no school had managed since Penn State in 1995.

No program had ever placed three players in the top four. The closest precedents were three picks inside the top five, done by Notre Dame in 1946, Alabama in 1948, Michigan State in 1967 and USC in 1977. Later that night tight end Jermaine Gresham went 21st to Cincinnati, giving Oklahoma four first-round picks in a single draft.

The pro careers backed up the hype. Bradford was the AP Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2010. McCoy made six straight Pro Bowls with the Buccaneers from 2012 to 2017. Williams kept stacking honors in Washington and San Francisco until he reached 12 Pro Bowl selections, one of only four offensive linemen in league history to get there.
So when the trivia question asks which school owned the top of the 2010 board, the answer is easy for any Sooner fan: Oklahoma, with three of the first four names.
